categories.title: Core protocol & reference
categories.blurb: The protocol's own repositories: canonical reference servers, the community registry, and the inspector you debug them with.

categories.title: Frameworks & SDKs
categories.blurb: Libraries for building an MCP server or client in your language, plus the frameworks that turn existing APIs into tools.

categories.title: Developer platforms & code
categories.blurb: Repositories, issues, design files and code intelligence — the servers a coding agent reaches for first.

categories.title: Databases & storage
categories.blurb: SQL, document, graph and vector stores, with the servers that query and administer them.

categories.title: Cloud & infrastructure
categories.blurb: Cloud providers, containers, infrastructure as code and observability stacks.

categories.title: Web, search & browsers
categories.blurb: Search APIs, crawlers and real browser control, for agents that need to read or operate the web.

categories.title: Productivity & business
categories.blurb: Notes, chat, tickets, mail, calendars and payments — the systems where work actually lives.

categories.title: AI, models & retrieval
categories.blurb: Model hubs, documentation retrieval and notebook access for agents that need external knowledge.

categories.title: Clients & hosts
categories.blurb: Applications that load MCP servers and hand their tools to a model, from desktop apps to IDE agents.

categories.title: Tools & utilities
categories.blurb: Inspectors, proxies, gateways and context helpers that sit around servers rather than replacing them.
